overarching.historical_origin: Convergence of Kaʻaheʻanua and Uxrowoiye after 1351 BCE
overarching.canonical_grammar: Approximately 90 percent particle-based, with SVO preferred and order flexibility when particles resolve meaning
overarching.identity_category_labels: not supplied; never synthesize labels from the count
overarching.general_word_endings: Vowel final preferred; inherited consonant-final words allowed
overarching.grammatical_gender: Do not infer gender from the 15 identity categories

eras.label: Proto Aza'raan
eras.order: SOV predominant; ritual verb-initial clauses possible
eras.profile: Convergence stage with vowel-dominant Kaʻaheʻanua syllables plus complex Uxrowoiye consonants and word-specific glottal/click letters
eras.particle_profile: Particles emerging; greater use of verbal endings and juxtaposition
eras.phonology: Vowel final base words, full historic W and clicking consonants; words may remain unsmoothed
eras.orthography: Independent historical glyphs and full sound-bearing characters, limited stacking
syntax_features: Head-final verb in ordinary narration
Postnominal descriptive phrases optional
Boundary glottal can differentiate adjacent vowels
Honorific position governed by ritual register
eras.status: proposed era grammar, with historical origin attested

eras.label: Ancient Aza'raan
eras.order: SOV neutral; SVO in contact or trade speech
eras.profile: Older separate sound letters persist; vowel repair increasingly regular
eras.particle_profile: Clause-role particles follow the words they mark; tense or aspect particles often attach at the end of the verb phrase
eras.phonology: Explicit /ʔ/ and click consonants; older Taz reading survives
eras.orthography: Separate independent phoneme signs, little or no compulsory subscript compression
syntax_features: Topic before other arguments
Object and recipient distinguished by following particles
Lexical and ritual stress not yet standardized
Identity markers are optional nominals, not compulsory gender agreement

eras.label: Archaic Aza'raan
eras.order: SOV and SVO in transition, differentiated by case and topic particles
eras.profile: Active shift from full historic alphabet to family-based accented letters
eras.particle_profile: A subset of role markers moves before its noun; TAM markers increasingly precede verbs
eras.phonology: Glottal and click still typeable as independent historical signs; consonant-contact vowel insertion codified
eras.orthography: Mixed independent letters and early subscripts; G/K/Q and B/F/V/W mergers begin in spelling
syntax_features: Preposed topic may dislocate a clause argument
Particle placement begins deciding argument order
Focused objects may precede the verb
Historical proper names remain conservative

eras.label: Classical Aza'raan
eras.order: SVO preferred; VSO permitted for formal or focused predicates
eras.profile: The 19-base family representation evolves, with B absorbing F/V/W, A family absorbing uh and O-family absorbing long oo; older letter forms remain historically documented.
eras.particle_profile: Most syntactic functions expressed by particles, with verbs carrying little agreement
eras.phonology: No independent glottal or click letters; glottal attaches before host, click after; vowel accents are obligatory for A family
eras.orthography: One base plus up to two subscripts; one accent for each letter; glottal-descended > and < emerge
syntax_features: Argument particles distinguish subject and object when order varies
Verb-initial ceremonial style is established
Inclusive and exclusive first-person distinctions are allowed
Plurality usually indicated by a particle rather than a stem change
eras.status: newly proposed grammar plus user-required script transition

eras.label: Traditional Aza'raan
eras.order: SVO neutral; focus fronting and VSO sacred register
eras.profile: Standardization of dependent vowels, gemination, honorific particles, subscript placement and compositional spelling
eras.particle_profile: Sentence-final evidential and politeness particles added, clauses can be linked by coordinators
eras.phonology: Strong open syllable preference; old codas and inherited Taz lexical readings protected
eras.orthography: Two-subscript stacking and one-accent-per-letter made standard
syntax_features: Demonstratives typically after the noun and determiners before
Aspect precedes main verb in neutral clauses
Negation takes a pre-verbal particle
Possession uses alienable and inalienable constructions

eras.label: Modern Aza'raan
eras.order: SVO default from canon; verb-initial VSO is a productive Māori-inspired marked construction
eras.profile: Māori-inspired spoken syllable composition with Khmer-inspired independent and stacked subscript letters
eras.particle_profile: Approximately 90 percent particle-based, temporal/aspect, number, location, direction, role, negation and focus expressed through particles
eras.phonology: (C)V(V) preferred, controlled epenthesis between consonants, automatic Nz and Tz repair; all old sounds preserved
eras.orthography: Exactly 19 independent letters ABDEGHIJKLMNOPRSTYZ; A-uh accent and O-oo accent; Khmer-inspired dependent vowel letters and up to two subscripts per host.
syntax_features: Verb-initial focus permits VSO without losing argument roles
Topic particles permit OSV or OVS when unambiguous
Flexible negation and tense-aspect-mood particles
Singular, dual, plural and inclusive/exclusive reference as Māori-inspired options
Noun phrase: optional determiner + noun + modifier + demonstrative
A zero gender agreement default avoids assigning binary categories to nouns
eras.status: user-directed new modern rules and source-aligned canon

continuity: Old words keep inherited pronunciations unless a lexicon entry explicitly records modernization
Each era is a synchronically distinct grammar, not just a font switch
The same text may have different era-appropriate order and spoken rendering
Sound family preservation is required at every historical transition
